description: A sine oscillator built on a two-state recurrence, with two outputs a quarter cycle apart and one control that pushes the tone towards harmonics and aliasing

params.text: Adds a fixed amount to the oscillator's running state every sample, 0 to 2, which bends the sine towards harmonics and aliasing; with the ALIASING jack patched it scales that voltage instead

inputs.text: Drives the shape amount from a voltage, a fifth of it multiplied by half the SHAPE knob, so the knob has to be off zero for this jack to do anything
Sets the pitch at 1V per octave, with 0V giving C4 at 261.63Hz

outputs.text: The main output, five times the sine of the running state
The quadrature output, five times the sine of the other state, a quarter cycle from the main one

notes: no pitch input is needed: with nothing patched to V/OCT the oscillator runs at C4
the oscillator resets its own state whenever the pitch changes at all, so a continuously moving V/OCT holds it at a standstill rather than sweeping it
